protocolMetadata.instructions:
Coverage Cat insurance MCP. This default server is intentionally the no-auth consumer/read-only surface: umbrella_consumer_prefill, homeowners_consumer_prefill, consumer_intake_issues, consumer_intake_patch, umbrella_consumer_select, umbrella_consumer_bind, umbrella_consumer_attach, umbrella_consumer_payment, umbrella_consumer_policy, umbrella_consumer_service, homeowners_consumer_select, homeowners_consumer_bind, homeowners_consumer_policy, and homeowners_consumer_service, plus read-only tools and embedded docs search. If Coverage Cat MCP tools are unavailable in a runtime that supports MCP, stop and ask a short choice question instead of telling the user to register `/.well-known/mcp.json` immediately.
Ask the question on its own line exactly as:

Would you like to install the Coverage Cat MCP (recommended) or use the REST/CLI tools instead?

Only share `/.well-known/mcp.json` after the user chooses MCP or asks for setup details. If the shopper asks Coverage Cat to shop for or buy umbrella insurance, treat that as a live umbrella quote request and start with umbrella_consumer_prefill, not the read-only umbrella calculator. For umbrella, stay on that same consumer subset through quoted offers, declarations upload, payment_needed, optional agentic payment collection, payment_url fallback, and post-bind policy/support follow-up; do not switch to delegated umbrella tools just to reach checkout or aftercare. When `payment_needed` appears, try `umbrella_consumer_payment` first before sending the shopper straight to `payment_url`. A shopper-safe umbrella sandbox also lives on this same subset: set sandbox: true only on the first umbrella_consumer_prefill call for a rehearsal, then keep using the same consumer tools through issues, patch, select, bind, attach, payment, policy, service, and status with synthetic quotes, uploads, payment credentials, policy records, and service-request results only. For homeowners, stay on the same consumer subset through review, long-lag q

tool.name: umbrella_consumer_prefill
tool.title: Umbrella consumer prefill handoff
tool.description: Preferred umbrella MCP entry point when a shopper wants Coverage Cat to shop for, compare, or buy umbrella insurance and no operator Bearer [redacted] is present. On a cold start, call this before asking the shopper a questionnaire. Assemble the fullest estimate you can justify from user-controlled context, let Coverage Cat stage the one-review handoff, and keep the user out of a step-by-step questionnaire. On the initial consumer umbrella handoff, prefer sending only intake; add top-level field_estimates only when you are certain each field already matches a current umbrella review field path. Use canonical consumer umbrella keys such as address.street, address.city, address.state, address.zip, license_state, license_number, approximate_asset_value or net_worth_numeric, desired_coverage_limit, required_coverage_e_limit, and vehicle_count or umbrella_details.motorized_vehicle_count for umbrella counts. Avoid top-level street/city/state/zip, drivers_license_state, drivers_license_number, net_worth, or desired_umbrella_liability_limit. Do not send vehicles rows before submission. Use vehicle_count or umbrella_details.motorized_vehicle_count for the household vehicle count; actual vehicle details are collected later only if a selected offer requires them, such as a Markel bind follow-up. Stay on the same consumer-operated MCP subset through quoted offers, declarations upload, payment_needed, optional agentic payment collection, payment_url fallback, and post-bind policy/support follow-up; do not switch to delegated tools just to reach checkout or aftercare. If you are rehearsing the shopper flow, set `sandbox: true` on this first prefill call only. That same consumer sandbox uid can then continue through `consumer_intake_issues`, `consumer_intake_patch`, `umbrella_consumer_select`, `umbrella_consumer_bind`, `umbrella_consumer_attach`, `umbrella_consumer_payment`, `umbrella_consumer_policy`, `umbrella_consumer_service`, and coarse `consumer_status` polling with synthetic quotes, uploads, payment credentials, policy outcomes, and service-request results only. Coverage Cat prefers to keep follow-up authorization in the hidden MCP shopper session after prefill, so a preserved host usually only needs uid. If your host cannot preserve that MCP session state, retry this same MCP follow-up tool with the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response instead of dropping to raw HTTP or asking the shopper for credentials. Until a later follow-up response shows quote progress, tell the shopper explicitly that the application is not submitted yet. When you summarize the staged review or remaining items, use short labeled bullets or sections rather than a prose paragraph. If any shown value is estimated, mark each estimated bullet label or value with `*`, include the short note `* = estimated` once above and once below the list, and do not prefix every estimated line with `[Estimated]`. Coverage Cat will not resume or expose a prior consumer umbrella draft based on email alone. Continue an existing consumer draft only through the issued uid plus the current hidden MCP session or latest intake_access_token handoff.

tool.title: Homeowners consumer prefill handoff
tool.description: Preferred homeowners MCP entry point when a shopper wants Coverage Cat to shop for, compare, or buy homeowners insurance and no operator Bearer [redacted] is present. On a cold start, ask only for the user's name, email, property address, and whether this should be standard homeowners, condo, or landlord coverage. If that coverage type is still unknown, ask the shopper to reply with exactly one of `standard homeowners`, `condo`, or `landlord`, then assemble the fullest homeowners application from user-controlled context and property sources before handing off to Coverage Cat. Recover core shopper and occupancy facts such as date of birth, marital status, and owner-occupied vs new-purchase from that context before relying on Coverage Cat's estimated review card. Stay on the same consumer-operated MCP subset through review, long-lag quote polling, quoted-offer selection, bind follow-up, and post-bind policy/support follow-up. Homeowners quotes or carrier bind follow-up may take up to 48 hours, so keep polling and keep the registered customer email on file for notifications. When the submitted homeowners flow gets a new follow-up question, consumer_intake_issues returns conversation.messages plus conversation.reply_pending so the agent can answer it in chat with consumer_intake_patch and message_reply. Coverage Cat prefers to keep follow-up authorization in the hidden MCP shopper session after prefill, so a preserved host usually only needs uid. If your host cannot preserve that MCP session state, retry this same MCP follow-up tool with the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response instead of dropping to raw HTTP or asking the shopper for credentials. Coverage Cat cannot collect first-party homeowners payment in chat. Any insurer payment or signing link must be sent directly to the customer's own email inbox on file, and the agent can only use those links if it has access to that same customer email. On the review turn, tell the shopper explicitly that the application is not submitted yet and present gathered details or remaining items as short labeled bullets or sections rather than a prose paragraph. If any shown value is estimated, mark each estimated bullet label or value with `*`, include the short note `* = estimated` once above and once below the list, and do not prefix every estimated line with `[Estimated]`.

tool.description: Continue a consumer-prefill homeowners or umbrella handoff in chat. Coverage Cat prefers to keep follow-up authorization in the hidden MCP shopper session after prefill, so a preserved host usually only needs uid. If your host cannot preserve that MCP session state, retry this same MCP follow-up tool with the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response instead of dropping to raw HTTP or asking the shopper for credentials. This follow-up tool stays in the default consumer-operated MCP subset; do not jump to delegated tools when no operator Bearer [redacted] is present. Before submission, say explicitly that the application is not submitted yet. Present gathered details, review facts, and remaining items as short labeled bullets or sections rather than a prose paragraph. If any shown value is estimated, mark each estimated bullet label or value with `*`, include the short note `* = estimated` once above and once below the list, and do not prefix every estimated line with `[Estimated]`. For homeowners, treat missing_fields as a hidden enrichment backlog, keep recovering core shopper and occupancy facts from user-controlled context, and reserve one final review turn. After submission, homeowners may also return conversation.messages, conversation.reply_pending, and reply_to_message_id so the agent can answer insurer or shopper follow-up in the same chat loop with consumer_intake_patch. For umbrella, keep missing fields hidden until Coverage Cat stages the single pre-submit review turn, then ask only for the explicitly missing shopper-owned fields in next_question and invite corrections to the reviewed facts instead of asking the shopper to re-key reviewed values before reading structured quotes and post-choose states. If the staged review shows a wrong estimated umbrella count from context, patch the canonical umbrella_details.* count field before you show the final review. Coverage Cat will not resume or expose a prior consumer umbrella draft based on email alone. Continue an existing consumer draft only through the issued uid plus the current hidden MCP session or latest intake_access_token handoff. Normalize shopper birthdays from MM-DD-YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD before you patch Coverage Cat.
